newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor, Nortel set terms on Telrad option.
newsitem.headline: Koor, Nortel set terms on Telrad option.

text.p: Koor Industries Ltd chief executive Benjamin Gaon said the company had agreed terms in principle with Northern Telecom Ltd on its option to buy 20 percent of Telrad.
The Canadian company has until the end of the year to exercise its option to buy 20 percent of Telrad, Koor's wholly owned telecommunications subsidiary, for $45 million.
"All the terms have been agreed," Gaon told Reuters.
But an accord has not yet been signed, he added.
"We will have the closing date at the end of October," Gaon said.
Koor is also considering floating Telrad shares in the U.S. market, but not before the end of 1997, Gaon said.
He said it was possible that Northern Telecom in the future would increase its stake in Telrad.

"They (Northern Telecom) asked in case we float the company they want to see equality, which means 50-50 at the end of the day. So there is a clause there (in the terms) that defines how we can reach such an equality in the future," Gaon said.
Gaon said he expects Telrad would be valued at about $800 million at the time of its flotation.
Koor, Israel's largest conglomerate, is also listed in New York.
